summaryText:
Pastor Travis Hearn continued the series My Wounds Won't Win with part two, titled Stop Bleeding on People. Building on the previous week's truth that we are not defined by our wounds, he explained that emotional pain tends to travel. When a heart is hurt, it can shape our conversations, marriages, friendships, parenting, and even our faith. People who are always offended, suspicious, or defensive are often reacting out of an unhealed wound. Pastor Travis warned that we can end up hurting people who never caused our pain, and that the enemy wants our wounds to affect families and future generations.

He shared three main ideas. First, unhealed wounds always leak. Using the story of Joseph, who was betrayed by his brothers, falsely accused, and forgotten, he showed that the real test of character is what comes out of us after we are hurt. He pointed to Luke 6:45, that the mouth speaks what the heart is full of. Second, healed people do not hide or deny their wounds, they surrender them to God. When Joseph later faced his brothers, he named the harm honestly, saying God intended it for good (Genesis 50:20). Pastor Travis taught that healing comes through revealing, not pretending, and that God turns open wounds into scars that carry a testimony. Third, healed people heal people. The greatest evidence of healing is not that we stop hurting, but that we stop hurting others. He encouraged the congregation to be transformed rather than to transfer pain (Romans 12:2), and to declare that the cycle stops with them.

Pastor Travis closed with a personal testimony about his mother. She faced deep heartbreak in her marriage and prayed daily for help to forgive. After about six months, she found her bitterness gone and was filled with peace and love, even helping to love and care for a child born from that painful situation. Her story showed what happens when we surrender hurt to God.

He then led the church in prayer, surrendering wounds to Jesus and inviting anyone who did not yet know Christ to give their life to him. The prayer team was available for those who wanted prayer. The church was encouraged to take time this week to pray, write down what stood out, ask God for a next step toward healing, and invite someone to join the rest of the series.
mainPoints: Unhealed wounds always leak: pain we refuse to bring to God will eventually spill onto the people around us, even those who never hurt us.
Healed people do not hide or deny their wounds, they surrender them to God, who turns open wounds into scars that tell a story of his redemption.
Healed people heal people: the evidence of healing is that we stop passing our pain on, so the cycle of hurt stops with us and God's transformation flows to the next generation.

versesMentioned.text: He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.
The tongue has the power of life and death, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.
Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!
A good man brings good things out of the good stored up in his heart, and an evil man brings evil things out of the evil stored up in his heart. For the mouth speaks what the heart is full of.
You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good to accomplish what is now being done, the saving of many lives.
Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what God's will is, his good, pleasing and perfect will.
For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life.

Monday.scripture: Psalm 147:3 (NIV): He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.
Monday.focus: Bringing your hurts honestly to the God who heals.
Monday.action: Set aside ten quiet minutes. Write down one hurt you have been carrying and tell God about it in your own words. If it feels heavy, consider sharing it with a trusted friend, pastor, or counselor.
Monday.prayer: Lord, I bring you the places in my heart that still hurt. I will not hide them from you. Heal what I cannot fix and bind up what is broken in me. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Luke 6:45 (NIV): For the mouth speaks what the heart is full of.
Tuesday.focus: Noticing where an old wound may be leaking into your words and reactions.
Tuesday.action: Pay attention today to moments when you feel defensive, offended, or quick to anger. Pause and take a slow breath before you respond. Write down what you notice and ask God what is underneath it.
Tuesday.prayer: Father, show me what is in my heart. Where my words and reactions reveal an old hurt, help me bring it to you instead of passing it on to others. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: Genesis 50:20 (NIV): You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good to accomplish what is now being done, the saving of many lives.
Wednesday.focus: Acknowledging the hurt honestly while trusting God to redeem it.
Wednesday.action: Write two sentences: one naming what happened and how it hurt, and one declaring that you trust God to bring good from it. Read both aloud as a prayer of surrender.
Wednesday.prayer: God, I do not pretend that it did not hurt. I surrender this pain to you and trust you to redeem it. Do not let my wound have the final word. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: Romans 12:2 (NIV): Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind.
Thursday.focus: Letting God's Word speak louder than the voice of the wound.
Thursday.action: Write down one discouraging message your wound has repeated to you. Next to it, write a truth from Scripture that answers it. Read the truth aloud morning and evening.
Thursday.prayer: Lord, renew my mind. Let your voice be louder than the voice of my past. Transform me by your power so I do not pass my pain on to others. Amen.

Friday.scripture: Ephesians 4:32 (NIV): Be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving each other, just as in Christ God forgave you.
Friday.focus: Asking God for help to forgive and to stop making others pay for old debts.
Friday.action: Pray each day this week for willingness to forgive the person who hurt you, even if you do not feel ready. If it is safe and wise, do one small act of kindness for someone else today, such as a kind message or word of thanks.
Friday.prayer: Jesus, I do not know how to forgive on my own. Help me. Soften my heart and keep me from making today's relationships pay for yesterday's hurts. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: 2 Corinthians 1:4 (NIV): Who comforts us in all our troubles, so that we can comfort those in trouble with the comfort we receive from God.
Saturday.focus: Letting your healing become a blessing to others.
Saturday.action: Encourage one person today with a call, a text, or a prayer. Consider inviting someone who may be carrying a quiet burden to join you for the next message in the series.
Saturday.prayer: God, thank you for the healing you are doing in me. Use my story to comfort others. Let the cycle of hurt stop with me and let your hope flow through my life. Amen.

title: How to Stop Hurting People With Your Unhealed Wounds | Stop Bleeding on People
